releases.displayName: Major Solarpunk update is finally here!

items.text: Hey Solarpunk Community!
It took a little longer than we originally hoped, but today we can finally say it: Solarpunk Update 1.3.0 is live!
This is our first bigger update since release and it brings a whole bunch of new features, content, improvements and fixes to the game.

We also want to say thank you for your patience and apologize for the long wait. Solarpunk is still being developed by a very small team. At the same time, every update needs to work not only on Steam, but across all console versions of the game as well.

That means new features and fixes need to be implemented, tested and verified across several different platforms before we can release them. It takes a little more time, but we want to make sure everyone gets the best version possible. But enough talking:
• Join sessions via invite codes
• View the player list directly from the in game menu
• Hosts can kick and ban players from their sessions
• Updated multiplayer UI for crossplay
1️⃣ Important for multiplayer: All players need to be on the same version in order to play together.
2️⃣ Console versions will receive this update a little later. We are currently waiting for approval and rollout by the console platform holders. This can take a few days.
• Added Lost Cargo drops that can appear during regular gameplay
• Lost Cargo can contain items such as the Big Chest, Roof Solar Panel, Wall Foliage, In Game Radio and Snap Connector
• Added map markers, messages and sound effects for Lost Cargo
• Reworked the chest system to support different storage sizes and names
• Added storage to nightstands, commodes and crates
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42064908/22e684cb061c584cff647d59fe86059221361e78.jpg"]
The Character Editor has received a major expansion with plenty of new customization options, giving you more freedom to create a character that feels uniquely yours.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42064908/b3fb3ea1b87da86a8b22cc80106264b3ee3c2e30.png"]
• Added a new UI Scaling option to the settings • UI scaling is now supported across several major interfaces • Nintendo Switch 2 and Steam Deck now default to the Large UI settin
• Removed the non shared worlds feature
• Added collectible postcards and a Postcard Pinboard to display your collection
• Added decorative flower patches, vines, ivy and glowing plants
• Added Sakura and Jacaranda trees
• Added an In Game Radio that plays the main menu soundtrack
• Added a new larger chest with increased storage capacity
• Added roof mounted solar panels
• Added connector holders for pillars and walls
• Added new fishing loot across different locations
• Increased the chance of fishing up cotton on the Starter Island
• Renamed the Algae Drone to Fishing Drone

• Fixed thunderstorms getting stuck in a loop for some players
• Fixed the Electrical Research Station not closing correctly with E or Tab
• Fixed the outdoor candle displaying the wrong state
• Fixed the Wooden Pillar in Glass Ring incorrectly requiring glass to build
• Fixed several typos
• Fixed save file names
• Fixed Character Editor settings not being reflected in the airship
• Added fallback achievement unlocking when loading a world
• Fixed the offset of the standing torch
• Fixed the Dock partly blocking placement of objects on itself
• Adjusted the Food Basket to unlock later, when it can actually be crafted
• Removed decorative pans from the Kitchen crafting recipe
• Added a system that automatically grants research unlocks players may have missed due to previous game updates
• Added a previously missing Alpha Backer credit
• Improved sign editor behavior and visuals
• Added an error message when kicking players fails
• Improved hover effects on the world type selector during world creation
Thank you again for playing Solarpunk and for sticking with us while we worked on this update. We hope you have fun exploring everything new in Version 1.3.0!
We’re already working on more features for Solarpunk, with a stronger focus on the ideas you’ve been submitting and voting for through our Feature Voting system.
We hear you want more content, more things to do, and that’s exactly what we want to build towards.

Right now, we’re working on things like an Airship overhaul, including support for multiple seats, as well as the ability to sit on furniture. Keep sending us your ideas and voting for your favorites. More soon! ❤️
We’re also planning the Farmers’ Market as a new hub for future content, quests, characters and adventures.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42064908/ce07c98cb293416655818dab31db1e2d5bf02177.png"]

If you enjoy Solarpunk and want to support us, a Steam review helps us enormously. No pressure, we completely understand if you want to wait. But every honest review helps us make the game more visible and continue working on it. Thank you to everyone who plays Solarpunk, shares feedback, submits ideas, and accompanies us on this journey. We truly appreciate it. 🌻
Best wishes
Cyberwave & rokaplay

releases.displayName: Solarpunk Update – Savegame Fix, Crossplay & Feature Voting

items.text: Hey everyone,
one week later, we want to give you another update.
A new Solarpunk update went live today. This update fixes a savegame issue that caused some players to lose save files or made them unable to load correctly.
To everyone who lost hours of progress because of this: we are truly sorry. This was a really nasty bug and a real beast, but we have hopefully managed to tame it now.
We saw that some of you were critical of the crossplay announcement because you mainly want more fixes and improvements. We understand that.
The important thing is: crossplay is being worked on in parallel. We are not stopping work on the game. Fixes, improvements, and new content are still being worked on.

While we switch to the new multiplayer system, we simply need to bundle updates more. This may make things look a little quieter from the outside, even though internally we are still working on many things.
The new system is not only meant to enable crossplay, but also to improve existing multiplayer issues — including cases where Steam players cannot reliably connect to each other.
In short: we are working on crossplay, still fixing issues, and preparing new content.

notes.title: We also want to remind you about our Feature Voting board

items.text: There you can submit feature requests and vote for ideas you would also like to see in Solarpunk.
This helps us a lot to understand which topics really matter to you and which community wishes are especially strong. It also helps us shape the upcoming roadmap better.
Some of the things already requested there were already on our to-do list. So upcoming updates will already include some first items from that list.
What exactly? You will see soon...
💬 Thank you for your feedback

Thank you to everyone who plays Solarpunk, gives feedback, reports bugs, submits ideas, and continues to support us. We know that not everything is perfect, but we keep working to improve Solarpunk step by step.
If you enjoy Solarpunk and want to support us, a Steam review helps us enormously.
No pressure — we completely understand if you want to wait. But every honest review helps us make the game more visible and continue working on it.
Thank you. 🌻
A project we like
Before we go, we also want to show you a project from friends of ours. If you like crafting games with wood, furniture, production lines, and a very different kind of chaos, please take a look at:

we released a small update with several fixes and improvements.

releases.displayName: 🌻 Solarpunk Mid-Update – Crossplay, Feature Voting & Small Fixes

items.text: Hey everyone,
we have a small mid-update for you.

Over the last few weeks, we have read many of your posts, reviews, bug reports, and feature requests. A lot of great ideas are coming in from the community, and we want to understand better which of them are most important to you.
One of the bigger topics we want to work on now is Cross-Platform Multiplayer.

The current multiplayer system is still strongly tied to the individual platforms. Our goal is that you will be able to play Solarpunk together across platforms in the future, no matter whether you are on PC, Xbox, PlayStation, or Nintendo Switch 2.
For us, this is not only an important feature by itself, but also a technical foundation for further ideas and future improvements.

Important: While we are working on this, we need to freeze our update intervals a little. As things stand now, we are not planning a larger update for roughly the next three weeks. Please do not take this as a fixed promise or exact date — with crossplay, something can always come up. But we want to be open with you about why updates will probably be a bit quieter during this time.
Of course, we will continue working on additional fixes and improvements in parallel.
We want to share a roadmap with you. However, we do not want to build it quietly behind closed doors and then simply say: “This is the plan now.”

The community has many different wishes: more decoration, more building pieces, more quality-of-life features, more animals, more plants, more automation, more multiplayer features, and much more. That is why we want to involve you more directly.
We have launched a Feature Voting System. There you can submit your own feature ideas and vote for existing suggestions:
LINK: https://solarpunk.featureupvote.com/
This helps us enormously to understand what really matters to you and which topics currently bring the most value to the community.
So if you have ideas: please use the voting system.
Add what you would like to see, and vote for the suggestions you would also like to have in the game.
This way, we can prioritize better and prepare the upcoming roadmap together with you.
🛠️ Small update / current fixes
There was also a small update with a few fixes and improvements:
Fixed animal type always showing as chicken for clients.
Possible fix for character editor settings not being replicated correctly.
Fixed gamepad navigation in the player inventory getting stuck in the hotbar after a backpack upgrade and opening a chest.
Adjusted the research description for Airship Dock V2.
Moved the “Unstuck” buttons from the settings into the in-game menu.
Moved the Socials button in the in-game menu further to the left.
Thank you to everyone who plays Solarpunk, gives feedback, reports bugs, joins discussions, and continues to support us. It really means a lot to us.

If you like Solarpunk and want to support us, a review still helps us enormously. No pressure — we completely understand if you would rather wait. But every honest review helps us make the game more visible and continue working on it.
Thank you. 🌻
Project we like
Before we go, we also want to show you a project from friends of ours. If you like crafting games with wood, furniture, production lines, and a very different kind of chaos, please take a look at:
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/4369130/Chop_Chop_Inc/"]
If it looks interesting to you, giving it a wishlist or follow would mean a lot to them. Thank you for supporting small indie games.

releases.displayName: 🌻 Solarpunk Update – What We Improved This Week

items.text: Hey everyone,
We are still working with full energy to improve Solarpunk. Our focus is still on fixes, stability, and issues that can directly affect your gameplay experience.
Some of the following points are classic bug fixes, while others are more improvements or small quality-of-life adjustments.
FIX for achievements not unlocking on clients.
FIX for achievements occasionally not unlocking on hosts.
FIX for achievements not unlocking on hosts when a client unlocks an achievement with shared progress or world relevance.
FIX: merchant input behavior was improved.
Added a new notification when a trade gives the player an airship upgrade.
Increased the duration of the death notification, as part of it was hidden by the transition.
Added a new “Unstuck Airship” button to the settings. This teleports the airship high into the air so it can then be called back to the dock.
FIX for inventory UIs becoming unresponsive with gamepad after a backpack upgrade. Currently fixed for: Chest, Furnace, Energy Furnace, Energy Generator, Postbox, and Recycler.
FIX for the virtual gamepad keyboard unintentionally opening in Steam Big Picture Mode after editing signs.
FIX for players not receiving the Diamond Achievement.
Added feedback to the postbox when there is no power.
Added a function that unlocks crafting recipes for players that they should already have unlocked through research. This should also fix the Beehive recipe bug, among other things.

We plan to send this update to the console platform holders at the beginning of next week. After that, the exact release timing on consoles depends on the respective platform review and approval process.
We know that not everything is perfect yet. We are still working on more fixes and are going through the open topics step by step.

At the same time, we are already thinking about the first upcoming features. However, we do not want to simply promise anything. Instead, we want to evaluate which things will bring the most value to you and to the game.

For this, we also want to use tools and possibly set up some kind of voting system, so we can better understand what the community wants most. A roadmap is also in progress. Please give us a little more time for this, as we want to prepare these things properly.
We read your reviews, your posts, and the forum. We cannot reply to everything directly, but we see a lot of it and take your feedback seriously.
Thank you to everyone who plays Solarpunk, reports bugs, shares feedback, and continues to support us 💘. It really means a lot to us. 🌻

notes.title: 💡 What Would You Like to See?

items.text: Until the voting system and roadmap are ready, feel free to already discuss here in the comments what you would like to see most in Solarpunk.

Which features would really help you? What would motivate you to stay longer in your world? And one thing we are especially interested in: Which decoration items, furniture, building parts, or small details would you like to see?
More plants? More lamps? Cozier furniture? More wall and floor options? More things for the farm or your houses?
Please share your wishes and ideas here. We read the posts. Really. It may be hard to believe, but we do. 🌻

And as always: If you like Solarpunk and want to support us, a review helps us enormously. No pressure — we completely understand if you want to wait a bit longer. But every honest review helps us make the game more visible and keep working on it. We are also really proud that the review score has reached 80%. Thank you so much.
Project we like

If it looks interesting to you, giving it a wishlist or follow would mean a lot to them. Thank you for supporting small indie games.

releases.displayName: Weekend Update – We are continuing to work on Solarpunk with full energy

items.text: Hey everyone,
we would like to give you a quick update before the weekend.

Right now, we are fully focused on improving Solarpunk. We also want to share a roadmap with you, but preparing something like that properly takes time — and at the moment, we are putting that time mainly into important fixes, stability, and issues that directly affect your gameplay experience.
So first, here is an overview of the most important things we fixed and improved this week.
Fixes
Added additional input prompts for changing rotation and height when building.
Fixed a backpack issue that could make the inventory unusable for clients in multiplayer.
Added a repair function for inventories that were corrupted by the backpack bug.
Fixed the Electronics Research Table UI not displaying researched items after reopening.
Fixed the merchant map marker appearing at the wrong position in the Airship Dock.
Fixed the radial menu being inverted when Y-axis inversion was enabled.
Fixed crop plots reappearing or duplicating after reloading a save.
Fixed the dough recipe not unlocking correctly after picking up wheat.
Fixed an issue that could cause players to fall through the Airship.
Improved or fixed Airship collisions and deaths when touching the Airship.
Updated the save state file naming convention.
World names now officially support language-specific characters and whitespace.
Added a migration system for save states created before version 1.0.3, ensuring compatibility with the new file naming convention.
Balancing & Improvements
The first melon and wheat plants now yield 2 seeds to help ease early game progression issues reported by the community.
Cotton now grows 25% faster to improve early game progression.
There are also a few smaller things included in the update, but these are the most important points from our perspective.

For Xbox and PlayStation players: Please be patient a little longer. The update first needs to go through the platform verification process. We hope this will move quickly. Nintendo Switch 2 users will need to be a little more patient.
We also want to say: We are here. We read your reviews, your posts, and your bug reports. Really. Our brains are burning right now, and the team is giving everything.
We currently still have 16 open A bugs that can noticeably affect the gameplay experience. Not everyone is affected by each of these bugs, but they have high priority for us.
So there is still a lot to do — but we will keep going.

Thank you to everyone who is playing Solarpunk, giving feedback, reporting bugs, and supporting us 💖. We are sorry for every bug that pulls you out of the game or frustrates you. We know that launch days are very intense, and we want to improve the game step by step.
And one small request: If you like Solarpunk and want to support us, a review helps us enormously. To the moon and back. 🌻
Of course, we also understand if you would rather wait or do not want to write a review right now. Your honest opinion matters.
We keep working.
Solarpunk Team

releases.displayName: 📅 Solarpunk: An Important Update About Our New Release Plan

items.text: Please read this text carefully!

[p align="start"]We know many of you have been waiting patiently for Solarpunk, and today we want to share an important update. Solarpunk means the world to us, but as a small two-person team, every detail takes
[p align="start"]time.

notes.title: We want to make sure it truly feels special when you finally get to play it, so we made the decision to move the release to next year.

items.text: [p align="start"]Over the past months, Solarpunk has grown beyond anything we could have imagined. We’ve now reached over 900,000 wishlists on Steam, had one of the most successful demos during Steam Next Fest in February with over 100,000 downloads, and our Kickstarter campaign was a huge success thanks to all of you. We’re incredibly proud of these milestones, but they also come with the pressure to deliver something truly great.

[p align="start"]One of the biggest parts of that is the multiplayer experience. Building a smooth, stable, and enjoyable co-op mode is one of the most complex challenges in game development. It takes extensive testing, fine-tuning, and a lot of time to make sure everything runs seamlessly for everyone. That’s why we decided to take a bit more time to ensure the multiplayer is as fun and reliable as the single-player experience you’ve already seen.

[p align="start"]Speaking of which, our single-player playtest was a huge success. 93% of testers said they would recommend the game, which makes us incredibly happy. It also helped us identify areas for improvement, and the upcoming multiplayer test will help us take the final steps before launch.

[p align="start"]This will be the final delay, and we can confidently say that Solarpunk is now entering its final phase. Thank you for your endless patience, your trust, and your excitement. You’ve supported us for years, and that means everything to us. We promise the wait will be worth it.
After the single-player playtest, we made some changes based on your feedback.
Inventory management: Players really want “craft from storage,” sorting options, and bigger stack sizes.
Airship controls: Some found flying a bit too sensitive and wished for an autopilot option for long trips.
Early-game pacing: Cotton grows too slowly and tools break too fast, making the early hours grindy.
Late-game goals: Players want more content, quests, and reasons to keep exploring.
Performance: Thunderstorms caused FPS drops and lightning bugs that sometimes hit players unfairly.
Animal systems: Some pathfinding issues caused animals to get stuck and stop producing.
Controller support: Needs more polish to fully support controller and Steam Deck play.
Tutorials: Players asked for clearer explanations for systems like electricity and crop sheltering.
[p align="start"]All of this feedback has been carefully reviewed, and many fixes and improvements are already in progress!
[p align="start"]We are currently preparing everything for the multiplayer playtest. The number of players who have access to the co-op mode will be gradually increased.
[p align="start"]We don't want to give a date (we haven't been very good at meeting deadlines in the past :P), but we will let you know very soon.
[p align="start"]With love and gratitude,
The Cyberwave Team 💛
If you're as passionate about cozy games as we are, we highly recommend subscribe to the cozy games newsletter.

releases.displayName: 🏠 Huge building system update, We won 2 OTK Awards, New Trailer

items.text: Hello Solarpunk Community 👋!

We've made significant advancements to our building system over the past few weeks, transitioning from collision channels to a tag-snap system. This gives users much more freedom when building their dream homes in Solarpunk.

notes.title: 📑 Summary of what we have done in the last weeks!

items.text: Building System

Changed the building system from collision channels to a tag snap system. So we theoretically have an infinite number of snap possibilities for example: Walls, roof slopes, columns, decorations, plants, electronic components and so on. Previously we were very limited in this respect.

There is now a system with which buildings can have special rules for building in individual cases. For example, carpets can be placed under furniture if the furniture is already in place. Wall shelves automatically rotate towards the wall so that they hang from it. Hanging plants can only be hung from the ceiling up to a certain angle and so on.

A system has been built in which ensures that buildables like decorations, cannot be built into each other. Due to a limitation in the Unreal engine, dynamic previews that have not yet been built can only have "simple collisions", which consist of boxes or similar simple shapes. However, we wanted it to be possible to place a candle on the edge of a furnace (for example). We therefore developed the system so that every buildable object has two possible collisions. A simple one for building and a complex (much more precise) one when the object is built. This way we can have the best of both worlds if necessary.
Building preview is no longer displayed if you have a placeable in your hand and a UI open
"Building rules" such as "Can only be built on land" or "Can only be built on water" have been added.

Floating water drone rework (which you can already see in the trailers). Now has floats that limit the area in which the drone fishes items out of the water and a box in which the drone brings the items, where you can then collect them as a player.
Sky environment improved. Clouds have been reworked. The sun now shines through the clouds better and adapts to the colour mood of the sun.
Weather system improved. Now have more control over weather changes and leaves and sticks fly through the air during thunderstorms

System prototyped so that you can be hit by whirling objects in a storm and take damage. It also takes into account the direction the wind is coming from, so you can take cover behind hills or walls from flying things.

notes.title: 🤗 We won a custom made PC & $10.000

items.text: During the OTK Games Expo, an event hosted by the Youtuber Asmongold, the community voted Solarpunk as "Best Trailer" and we won $10.000. We also won an Award for "Most unique Artstyle" and we will receive a custom made Solarpunk-themed PC from Starforge System. Over 300.000 people watched the event live and we are so incredibly grateful for our community. You are amazing 😍!
In the light of the Games baked in Germany Steam event we have created a new trailer. You can watch it here.
We hope you enjoyed the news here and leave us a comment or your opinion on what you would like to know in the next update.
You can always join our Dev-Discord and ask us what we are currently working on.
Best regards
Cyberwave & rokaplay Team

releases.displayName: Dev-Update: Airship facelift + new flight physic

items.text: Hey Solarpunk community!
We're back with another exhilarating update on the Solarpunk frontier! 🌞✈️
We have adjusted the look of the airship. Among the new features are the ingenious directional propellers, which are now clearly visible in 3rd person mode.
Get ready to fly through the skies in style! 🌪️ Check out the stunning visual overhaul in the attached images.
Remember that Dock concept we teased last time?
Well, buckle up, because it's officially in the game! You can upgrade your airship at the dock. The airship will land automatically as soon as you are near it and press the docking-button.

We have also reworked the flight physics. The airship now flies much more comfortably. Fun fact: At the time we produced the trailer, the flying was extremely spongy and not polished at all. But it was enough for the trailer :D
Take a look at the dock + the flight physics in this little clip.

The airship now has a damage system. If you're not careful and hit something, it takes damage. From 50% damage it starts to smoke and is much more difficult to steer. If the damage reaches 100% or you crash directly into a wall at high speed, it breaks immediately. You will be able to craft repair kits to repair your airship. The hull can be upgraded later in the game so that the airship doesn't break so quickly.
🚧 A lot of what you see is still WIP and may differ from the final product! 🚧
In case you're wondering what all the Buttons/indicators mean, here's an explanation for those who like lists :).
Forward speed
Reverse gear
Upper lamp: Indicates whether you can dock in the open. (Works everywhere as long as the airship is stationary and relatively straight. You can also dock in mid-air, for example)
Lower lamp: Indicates if you can dock at a dock (if the dock is within a radius of approx. 5 meters, you can dock there automatically)
Battery / Solar panel
Battery is charged by the solar panel when exposed to sunlight
Charges less quickly in the morning and evening than in the midday sun
Also dependent on the weather. In the rain it charges slowly, in sunshine it charges quickly
If covered by shade, also less charging power
Flying consumes battery
The faster you fly, the more energy the airship needs
The small rotors also consume energy

Light also consumes energy. (If you land at night and forget to switch off the light, your battery runs down because the solar panel does not charge the battery at night. So you shouldn't forget to switch the lights off again. Just like in a car)
Solar charging indicator Indicates whether the battery is currently being charged or not
Altitude indicator
Shows how far the airship is from the minimum and maximum altitude
If the altitude is too low or too high, the autopilot switches on and automatically pulls the airship up/down again
Camera
Free look around while flying
1st/3rd person camera
Things that are not available from the start, but can be upgraded as the game progresses
Chest: The chest is not in the airship from the start, and you have to install it first

Holographic display: The Holo HUD is currently still very wip. It will show additional information such as exactly how much power is being consumed, how much the solarpanel charges and other information such as the level of damage taken, flight altitude, time, etc
Battery storage can be upgraded
Solar panel charging speed can be upgraded
Engine (more speed)
Hull (less damage from collisions)
Balloon can be upgraded so that you can fly higher overall with the airship
